name: Treaty with the Sauk and Foxes, 1842
aka: Treaty of the Sac and Fox Agency (1842)
promises: In return for all Sauk and Fox land west of the Mississippi, interest of five per cent a year on $800,000, and payment of the tribes' listed debts of $258,566.34 (Article 2).
The President to assign the tribes a tract on the Missouri River or its waters for a permanent and perpetual residence (Article 2, First).
Blacksmith and gunsmith shops to be moved and kept up, and provisions furnished for the removal and for up to a year after arrival, charged to the tribes' funds (Articles 2 and 3).
The tribes could stay for three years on the western part of the cession, west of a line from the Red Rocks on the White Breast fork of the Des Moines River (Articles 1 and 3).

breaches.what: The Indian Claims Commission found that the Sauk and Fox share of Royce Area 262 (8,592,000 acres in central Iowa) was worth $12,028,800 when this treaty took effect on February 15, 1843, held that the consideration the tribes received was unconscionable, and awarded $10,601,282.66 after crediting payments under this treaty and an 1837 treaty.

breaches.quote: The consideration received by the Sac and Fox for their lands was unconscionable.

breaches.what: The Meskwaki Nation's chronology of the removal records that settlers crossed the Mississippi to squat on Sac and Fox land before the June 1, 1833 removal deadline of an earlier treaty, that removal treaty talks failed in 1840 and that the tribes refused an 1841 offer, and that dragoons were sent in 1845 and 1846 to escort Meskwaki who had not left Iowa under this treaty.

source.title: A Narrative of Chronology and Perspectives on the Removal and Return of the Meskwaki to Iowa, 1839-1857

landTaken: Royce Area 262 contains 11,776,000 acres; the Commission found the Sauk and Fox held recognised title to 8,592,000 acres of it (262 North) and the Iowa Nation to the other 3,184,000 acres (Docket 153, Findings of Fact 15, 1970). The cession also covered any other Sauk and Fox land west of the Mississippi.
compensation: The Commission credited the United States with $1,341,446.34 under this treaty (including $800,000 as the value of the five per cent interest it treated as a perpetual annuity) and $86,071 under the Missouri Sauk and Fox treaty of October 21, 1837, and awarded the Sac and Fox Nation $10,601,282.66 on February 4, 1970.
today: Some Meskwaki stayed in or returned to Iowa; Iowa passed a law in 1856 letting them remain, and they bought their first 80 acres in Tama County on July 13, 1857 (Meskwaki Nation history). Those removed went to a reservation in east-central Kansas (Meskwaki Nation history).

plain.promised: Five per cent a year on $800,000, payment of $258,566.34 in tribal debts, and a permanent and perpetual home on the Missouri River or its waters, for all Sauk and Fox land west of the Mississippi.
plain.happened: The Indian Claims Commission found in 1970 that 8,592,000 acres in central Iowa were worth $12,028,800 and that the tribes' consideration was unconscionable. The Meskwaki Nation records dragoons sent in 1845 and 1846 to escort Meskwaki out.
plain.today: The Commission awarded the Sac and Fox Nation $10,601,282.66 in 1970; whether it was paid has not been traced. Some Meskwaki stayed and bought their first 80 acres in Tama County in 1857.

nationVoice.nation: Meskwaki Nation (Sac and Fox Tribe of the Mississippi in Iowa)
nationVoice.summary: The Meskwaki Nation's own chronology of the 1839-1857 removal and return gathers eyewitness, agency and government records of the 1842 negotiations, the removal under this treaty and the families who stayed or came back to Iowa.

nationVoice.nation: Meskwaki Nation (Sac and Fox Tribe of the Mississippi in Iowa)
nationVoice.summary: The Nation's history page says the Sauk and Meskwaki lost all their Iowa lands through a series of concessions by 1845 and were removed to Kansas, while an unbroken Meskwaki presence remained in Iowa.

openQuestions: The queue lists Royce Areas 262, 419 and 494 for this id; 419 and 494 appear to be the Kansas lands assigned to the tribes after this treaty and ceded later (1859, 1867). Only Royce 262 was covered by the Docket 153 award.
The Commission's opinion (pointer 2184) was read only in part; its reasons for treating the five per cent interest as a perpetual annuity worth $800,000 were not checked line by line.
The Meskwaki chronology quotes an 1846 account saying some fifteen hundred Sauk and Fox were still in Iowa after the removal deadline; that figure is the account's, not verified here.

Audit 2026-11-08: Docket 153 figures, the quote and the treaty articles held. The nation-statement text was tightened to what the Meskwaki chronology actually says (squatters before the 1833 deadline, failed 1840 talks, refusal in 1841, dragoons in 1845-46). 'today' no longer names the Sac and Fox Nation of Missouri, which descends from the Missouri band (treaty of October 21, 1837), not from this treaty's parties, and the Oklahoma successor was not sourced in this file.
